source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 11: total work of three constant forces equals 102 Nm (book p.275). Verified; the key gives no separate answer.

blocks.prompt: 11. A particle is displaced from the point \(A(5, -5, -7)\) to the point \(B(6, 2, -2)\). Under the action of constant forces defined by \(10\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 11\underline{k}\), \(4\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + 9\underline{k}\) and \(-2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 9\underline{k}\). Show that the total work done by the force is 102 Nm.
blocks.explanation:
Three constant forces act together; we must show that the total work is 102 Nm.
Plan: add the three forces, find \(\underline{AB}\), take the dot product and compare with 102.
steps:
Given: forces \(10\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 11\underline{k}\), \(4\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + 9\underline{k}\), \(-2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 9\underline{k}\); displacement from \(A(5, -5, -7)\) to \(B(6, 2, -2)\).
To prove: total work \(= 102\) Nm.
Method: Work done by a constant force \(W = \underline{F}\cdot\underline{d}\) (14.2.8), where \(\underline{d}\) is the displacement vector from the starting point to the end point. Use the resultant of the three forces.

Resultant force
\[\underline{F} = (10 + 4 - 2)\underline{i} + (-1 + 5 + 1)\underline{j}\]
\[\quad + (11 + 9 - 9)\underline{k}\]
\[= 12\underline{i} + 5\underline{j} + 11\underline{k}\]
Why: Forces acting together add as vectors.

Displacement
\[\underline{d} = (6 - 5)\underline{i} + (2 + 5)\underline{j} + (-2 + 7)\underline{k}\]
\[= \underline{i} + 7\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\]
Why: \(\underline{AB}\) = end point minus starting point.

Check: each force separately
\[(10, -1, 11)\cdot(1, 7, 5) = 10 - 7 + 55 = 58\]
\[(4, 5, 9)\cdot(1, 7, 5) = 4 + 35 + 45 = 84\]
\[(-2, 1, -9)\cdot(1, 7, 5) = -2 + 7 - 45 = -40\]
\[58 + 84 - 40 = 102 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The works of the separate forces add up to the same total.
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: total work done \(= 102\) Nm.
